validity.researcher_notes: DIAMETER DISCREPANCY sourced directly to the FERC certificate order's segment-by-segment facilities description, the single most granular source found: 'a 2.79-mile extension of the 36-inch-diameter Ventura North E-line (Segment 1); a 1.07-mile, 30-inch-diameter loop of the 20-inch-diameter Elk River 1st and 2nd branch lines (Segment 2); a 1.14-mile extension of the 24-inch-diameter Willmar D branch line (Segment 3); a 2.48-mile extension of the 8-inch-diameter Princeton tie-over loop (Segment 4); a 2.01-mile 4-inch-diameter loop of the 3-inch-diameter Paynesville branch line (Segment 5); a 0.34-mile extension of the 8-inch-diameter Tomah branch line loop (Segment 6)'. Reading this carefully: Segment 2's NEW pipe is 30-inch-diameter; the '20-inch-diameter' clause describes the EXISTING Elk River branch line being paralleled/looped, not new construction. Segment 5's NEW pipe is 4-inch-diameter (looping an existing 3-inch line). So the new-build diameter set is {36, 30, 24, 8, 4, 8} = distinct values {4, 8, 24, 30, 36} -- the sheet's recorded '20' does not belong in a new-construction diameter list, and '4' (the smallest genuinely new pipe) is missing from it. The NOI to prepare an EIS (FR-2022-08-03/2022-16589) independently corroborates the 4-inch figure: 'a 2.01-mile loop of 4-inch-diameter Paynesville Branch Line...(Paynesville 2nd Branch Line)'. Staged at medium/independent:false (single strong FERC-docket origin, the NOI corroborates but is the same FERC-docket origin per this slice's counting rule) diverging from EIA's existing figure, matching the same tier-discipline treatment used for the Length concern above.
